newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's UM sees 30 pct drop in 1st half profit.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's UM sees 30 pct drop in 1st half profit.

text.p: Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere SA (UM) on Tuesday put a brave face on a 30 percent drop in first half profits and said the future was starting to look brighter.

It said group net profit fell 29.9 percent to 218 million francs in the six months to June 30 from 311 million ($10 million) in the same period last year, as the depressed state of the European construction industry more than outweighed an improved performance in recycling and zinc and copper refining.

Chief Executive Officer Karel Vinck, shrugging off the decline, told reporters the restructuring plan UM put in place in January was going well and that, all things being equal, the second half year would be better than the first,
"Our industrial plan is totally on track. There is a good spirit of collaboration and cooperation with the unions," he told a news conference.
Vinck said the metals recycling business based on Hoboken in the Netherlands had performed well as had the copper and zinc refining activities.
In the so-called transformation division, the company had great hopes for its cobalt production for use in rechargeable batteries and its germanium production for use in solar panels.

The building products section of this division, however, which makes zinc sheet, had been mauled by the depressed state of the construction industry in Europe -- particularly in Germany and France but also to a lesser extent in Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

"In each of these three divisions the industrial plan is on Track," Vinck said. He stressed that the effects of the plan would not be felt at all in the 1996 figures but would start to feed through from 1997 onwards.
"A summary of the first half shows the negative results all influenced by building products," he said.
Vinck said the firm expected metals prices and the dollar to remain stable for the rest of the year and interest rates to remain low.
The market outlook for some of its speciality metals such as cobalt looked rosy, although there were mixed views on the likely performance of the building products sector, he said.

Vinck also noted that such was the mood of confidence that UM's board of directors had agreed on Tuesday to add an extra 150,000 tonnes per year more copper refining capacity at a cost of 1.3 billion francs, taking the total new capacity to 350,000 tonnes at an investment cost of four billion francs.
"Overall we feel that the second half will be better that the first half," Vinck said.
UM made a group net loss of 954 million francs in full year 1995 but a current profit of 1.8 billion. ($1=31.09 Belgian Franc)
